correctness.rationale: In a proper coloring a mixed color confined to one paired block cannot coexist with a pure side color in a b-coloring; multiple pure same-side colors have no CDVs; two mixed colors in the same block have no mutual CDV. These exhaustive cases yield precisely the bipartition and paired-block colorings, each with every vertex a CDV for r>=3. The sorted sequence inequalities and profile realization follow. Exhaustive independent edge and closed-neighborhood verification passes on 10 varied graph profiles. No finite check is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating recently introduced invariant asks which sequences a fixed graph realizes. This gives all b-colorings and exact CDV-multiplicity profiles for every connected graph in a natural parameterized class of bipartite biclique-edge complements, a full structural classification. Every list of nontrivial color-multiplicities w_i>=2 can be realized with an arbitrary gap between the only two admissible numbers of colours; the weighted profile result exceeds the known unweighted two-point gap. No general downstream theorem is claimed.
